newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's VEW - expects higher 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Germany's VEW - expects higher 1997 earnings.

text.p: German energy group VEW AG said on Tuesday it expected a further improvement in earnings in the current year after it reported a 12.5 percent rise in 1996 net profits to 281 million marks ($162.4 million).
"After a good start in the current business year we expect to raise profits again in 1997 given continued improvement in the economic environment," the company said in its annual report.
VEW also said that it expected its dividend for 1997 to at least match 1996. The group raised its 1996 dividend payout by 50 pfennigs to 9.50 marks.
"Otherwise we wouldn't have raised the 1996 dividend figure," Fritz Ziegler, management board chairman of VEW, told the group's annual news conference.
Ziegler declined to give a definite earnings prognosis and said it was difficult to calculate whether or not the group would again register double-digit growth rates.
The group said that the harsh winter at the start of 1996 helped boost energy sales, but said that energy sales in the first quarter of 1997 were lower.
VEW said it still hopes to lift group sales to nine billion marks in 1997 from 8.7 billion marks last year.
Overall group sales during the year were slightly higher at 8.586 billion marks in 1996 compared to 8.546 billion marks in 1995.
Electricity sales fell to 43.2 billion kilowatt hours in 1996 from 43.6 billion kilowatt hours the previous year, while gas sales increased to 43 billion kilowatt hours from 37.8 billion.
Ziegler said that the group's waste disposal unit, Edelhoff, would return to profitability in 1997.

"We are sure that we will reach our targets," he said, referring to the waste disposal group which again reported losses in 1996 at 29 million marks, compared to losses of 21 million the previous year.
Sales in VEW's waste disposal business were 898 million marks in 1996, up slightly from 873 million marks.
Ziegler also said that it wanted to take a stake in the Westphalian gas group WFG, by transferring part of its gas business into WFG.
Shares in VEW were lower during bourse trade in Frankfurt on Tuesday, down two marks at 498 marks, while the overall market was up 20.59 points, or 0.61 percent, at 3,383.65 points.
